causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand in New South Wales peaked at a summer record of 13 567 MW at 2 pm, 300 MW greater than that forecast four hours ahead.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: The majority of this reduction was a result of unplanned outages and delays in returning generation plant to service.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: On 15 January, the Lower Tumut to Upper Tumut 64 line was out for service as part of a 12 day planned network outage that commenced on 5 January.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: At the time around 1170 MW, or 9 per cent of available capacity in New South Wales was priced above $5000/MWh, 890 MW of which was from rebidding by participants.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Total import capability into New South Wales was around 290 MW lower than forecast four hours ahead.

interconnectors_named.name: QNI
interconnectors_named.quote: The QNI import limit was close to forecast.

interconnectors_named.name: Terranora interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Outages of equipment associated with the Terranora interconnector reduced import capability below nominal levels.

intervals.quote: On 15 January 2009, the spot market price in New South Wales exceeded $5000/MWh for the 2 pm trading interval.

network_outages.quote: In addition, around 2100 MW of generation in New South Wales was unavailable and planned network outages led to reduced import capability.

peak_price.quote: On 15 January the spot price in New South Wales reached $5210/MWh at 2 pm.

rebid_set_price.quote: The resulting tight supply-demand balance coupled with rebidding by New South Wales generators saw the spot price reach $5210/MWh.
